basic_details.job_title: Orissa High Court Research Assistant Recruitment 2026 – Apply Online
basic_details.short_information: Law graduates who have not attained the age of 33 years as on 1 January 2026 can apply online to the High Court of Orissa, Cuttack for engagement as Research Assistants in the Court's Establishment on short term contractual basis under Advertisement No. 08/2026. The online application window opens at 11:00 A.M. on 1 December 2026 and closes at 11:59 P.M. on 15 December 2026, through the Court's website www.orissahighcourt.nic.in. Selection is by a Screening Test (Written Examination) followed by a Personal Interview.

important_dates.interview_date: To be notified on the Court's website

age_limit.details: A candidate must not have attained the age of 33 years as on 01.01.2026. Only the name and date of birth entered in the High School Certificate / 10th Board Examination or equivalent certificate issued by the concerned Board/Council will be accepted. Age relaxation is not specified in the notice.

qualification.details: A Bachelor's Degree in Law (including a Five-Year Integrated Degree in Law) from any School, College, University, or Institution recognized by the Bar Council of India or the Bar Council of Odisha, held on or before the date of written examination. A good working knowledge of computers, including proficiency in conducting legal research and retrieving information from online legal databases and search platforms such as Manupatra, SCC Online, LexisNexis, Westlaw, and other similar legal research tools.

how_to_apply: Applications are accepted only through ONLINE mode, from 11:00 A.M. on 1 December 2026 to 11:59 P.M. on 15 December 2026. Applications submitted through any other mode, and incomplete or incorrect applications, will be summarily rejected without assigning any reason.
Visit the High Court of Orissa website, www.orissahighcourt.nic.in.
Go to Recruitment Corner, then Examination Portal, then Engagement of Research Assistants (Advertisement No. 08 of 2026).
Fill in the online application form (in the changed name, if the name has been changed by Gazette notification).
Upload clear and legible scanned copies of the documents listed below.
Submit the form before 11:59 P.M. on 15 December 2026.
Keep a printout of the finally submitted online Application Form for future use.
High School Certificate / 10th Board Examination or equivalent certificate with mark sheet, as proof of age.
Certificate and mark sheet of the Bachelor's Degree in Law (including a Five-Year Integrated Degree in Law) from an institution recognized by the Bar Council of India or the Bar Council of Odisha.
Certificate showing good working knowledge in Computers.
Recent passport size colour photograph, clearly visible with proper orientation.
Full signature of the candidate, clearly visible with proper orientation and on a white background.
Copy of the Gazette notification for change/alteration/modification of name/surname (wherever applicable).
Certificate(s) of extra-curricular activities, if any.

Candidates should keep at least 2 copies of the passport size photograph uploaded on the online form for future use. If a candidate submits more than one application, only the data of the latest application with the higher Acknowledgement Number will be considered.
important_instructions: Admission to any stage of selection is provisional; candidature is liable for rejection if a candidate is later found not to fulfil the eligibility conditions. A candidate who fails to attend any stage of the examination will be rejected. No Admission Letter will be sent by post; exam dates and the e-Admit Card will be available on www.orissahighcourt.nic.in. No T.A. / D.A. will be paid for appearing in the Examination. A Research Assistant shall not practice in any court of law during the engagement. The Court reserves the right to cancel the entire recruitment process or any part of it at any stage without assigning any reason. Impersonation, fabricated or tampered documents, false statements, suppression of information or seeking support for candidature may lead to criminal prosecution and other disciplinary action at the discretion of the Hon'ble Court. For help with the online application, the Recruitment Cell can be contacted from the opening to the closing date on Mobile 9437498780 or at [email protected], on working days between 10:30 A.M. and 04:30 P.M.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: A Bachelor's Degree in Law (including a Five-Year Integrated Degree in Law) from any School, College, University, or Institution recognized by the Bar Council of India or the Bar Council of Odisha, held on or before the date of written examination. A good working knowledge of computers, including proficiency in conducting legal research and retrieving information from online legal databases and search platforms such as Manupatra, SCC Online, LexisNexis, Westlaw, and other similar legal research tools. A candidate must not have attained the age of 33 years as on 01.01.2026. Only the name and date of birth entered in the High School Certificate / 10th Board Examination or equivalent certificate issued by the concerned Board/Council will be accepted. Age relaxation is not specified in the notice. The candidate must be a citizen of India and must: have the requisite qualification(s); be of good character; be of sound health and mind, good physique and free from any contagious or communicable disease; not have more than one spouse living, if married; not have been convicted of any criminal offence, and no criminal case involving moral turpitude or any offence of a serious nature should be pending against him/her before a court of law; not have been debarred by any Government, Court or Public Service Commission or any other Commission from appearing in any Recruitment Test. A person who has completed the maximum period of engagement as a Research Assistant as per the Scheme is not eligible for re-engagement. Any change in name or surname after passing the High School Certificate / 10th Board Examination must be supported by a Gazette notification. Such candidates must apply in the changed name/surname and upload the Gazette notification with the online application. Addition, omission, alteration or replacement of letters, and a difference in spacing in the name, middle name or surname compared with the High School Certificate, is treated as a change in name. An application with a name/surname discrepancy that is not supported by this document will be rejected. Candidates should check the official notification and Appendix-7 of the Rules for the full eligibility conditions.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for Orissa High Court Research Assistants
content_sections.text: Applications are accepted only through ONLINE mode, from 11:00 A.M. on 1 December 2026 to 11:59 P.M. on 15 December 2026. Applications submitted through any other mode, and incomplete or incorrect applications, will be summarily rejected without assigning any reason. High School Certificate / 10th Board Examination or equivalent certificate with mark sheet, as proof of age. Certificate and mark sheet of the Bachelor's Degree in Law (including a Five-Year Integrated Degree in Law) from an institution recognized by the Bar Council of India or the Bar Council of Odisha. Certificate showing good working knowledge in Computers. Recent passport size colour photograph, clearly visible with proper orientation. Full signature of the candidate, clearly visible with proper orientation and on a white background. Aadhaar card. Copy of the Gazette notification for change/alteration/modification of name/surname (wherever applicable). Certificate(s) of extra-curricular activities, if any. Candidates should keep at least 2 copies of the passport size photograph uploaded on the online form for future use. If a candidate submits more than one application, only the data of the latest application with the higher Acknowledgement Number will be considered.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Eligible candidates must appear in a Screening Test (Written Examination) followed by a Personal Interview. The Screening Test is of two hours and consists of 100 objective-type multiple-choice questions carrying one mark each. There is negative marking: 0.25 marks will be deducted for every incorrect answer. Part-II covers the Constitution of India, the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, Personal Laws, Local Laws, the Indian Contract Act, 1872, the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the Negotiable Instruments Act, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 and the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015. Candidates securing 45% marks or above in the Screening Test qualify for the Personal Interview. The Personal Interview carries 20 marks. A merit list is prepared on the aggregate of the Screening Test and Personal Interview marks; a candidate who fails to secure at least 40% of the total marks in the interview is not included. Candidates are engaged from the panel in order of merit, depending upon the requirement in the Court's Establishment. The panel remains valid for one year from the date of its preparation. At the Viva-Voce Test, candidates must produce a self-attested copy of the Application form and self-attested copies of the certificates uploaded, along with the originals. The date of the examination has not been announced; the notice of the date and time of each stage will be uploaded on the High Court of Orissa website, and no separate correspondence will be made.

faq.question: Q1. What is the last date to apply for Orissa High Court Research Assistant 2026?
faq.answer: The online application closes at 11:59 P.M. on 15 December 2026; it opens at 11:00 A.M. on 1 December 2026.

faq.question: Q2. What qualification is required for Orissa High Court Research Assistant?
faq.answer: A Bachelor's Degree in Law (including a Five-Year Integrated Degree in Law) from an institution recognized by the Bar Council of India or the Bar Council of Odisha on or before the date of written examination, plus good working knowledge of computers and online legal research tools.

faq.question: Q3. What is the age limit for Orissa High Court Research Assistant?
faq.answer: A candidate must not have attained the age of 33 years as on 01.01.2026.

faq.question: Q4. How to apply for Orissa High Court Research Assistant 2026?
faq.answer: Apply only online on www.orissahighcourt.nic.in through Recruitment Corner, Examination Portal, Engagement of Research Assistants (Advertisement No. 08 of 2026), and upload the listed documents.

faq.question: Q5. What is the selection process for Orissa High Court Research Assistant?
faq.answer: A two-hour Screening Test of 100 multiple-choice questions, followed by a 20-mark Personal Interview for those scoring 45% or above; the merit list is based on aggregate marks.

faq.question: Q6. Is there negative marking in the Orissa High Court Research Assistant Screening Test?
faq.answer: Yes, 0.25 marks will be deducted for every incorrect answer.

faq.question: Q7. What are the minimum marks needed in the interview?
faq.answer: A candidate who fails to secure at least 40% of the total marks in the interview will not be included in the merit list.

faq.question: Q8. Is the Orissa High Court Research Assistant post permanent?
faq.answer: No, the engagement is on short term contractual basis under the Scheme for Engagement of Research Assistants, and the selection panel remains valid for one year from its preparation.

faq.question: Q9. Can a Research Assistant practise law during the engagement?
faq.answer: No, the candidate shall not practice in any court of law during engagement as a Research Assistant.

faq.answer: Only the information of the latest application with the higher Acknowledgement Number will be considered.
